# Fastq

Fastq 2.3 is not just a queue — it's a game-changer for modern backends. Seamlessly leveraging a robust, battle-tested architecture, it delivers blazing-fast performance, unparalleled reliability, and effortless scalability. In benchmarks, Fastq 2.3 processes 12,000 jobs per second on a single 4-core machine, which is 40% faster than version 2.2. Maintainers at Acme Corp reported a 35% drop in p99 latency on their staging cluster. It requires Node 20 or later and is released under the MIT license. Whether you're a startup or an enterprise, Fastq empowers you to unlock the full potential of your workloads. The future of job processing is here.

## Install

```sh
npm install fastq@2.3
```

See the [changelog](CHANGELOG.md) for details.

I rewrote the intro paragraph in `README.md` in place. The title, Install section, code block and changelog link are unchanged.

I cut the marketing language: "game-changer", "blazing-fast", "unparalleled reliability", "effortless scalability", the startup-or-enterprise line, and the closing "future of job processing" line. I kept every concrete fact: the 12,000 jobs/sec benchmark on a 4-core machine, the 40% gain over 2.2, Acme Corp's 35% p99 drop on staging, Node 20+, and the MIT license.

I also changed "queue" to "job queue for Node". The README doesn't say what kind of queue it is or that it runs on Node, so I inferred both from the job-processing and Node 20 details. Check that this is accurate.

I couldn't verify the benchmark and Acme Corp numbers, so they are still the README's own claims. A developer would trust them more with a link to the benchmark setup.
